anna: Heads-up — I noticed a sharp drop in prefix cache hit-rate after yesterday's kernel selection change + the tiny tokenizer micro-patch. p95 for chat routes crept up and route-level hit-rate fell across tier-1 models. posting quick numbers and ideas below.

miguel: numbers? which routes are worst?

anna: aggregated hit-rate before: ~78%. after: ~44%. tool-heavy routes are worst (down to ~28%). profiler shows KV payloads ~1.6x larger on average which looks like different serialization/chunk alignment after the kernel swap. also seeing more frequent small-evictions in the warmup window.

sam: do we know if tokenizer IDs changed or if the keying algo changed?

anna: tokenizer package version is identical, but the micro-patch changed how zero-width/whitespace siblings are normalized (we used to strip a zero-width NBSP in the canonicalizer; new patch preserves it). important bit: our cache key is computed over the serialized prompt + tool fields string that the runtime produces post-kernel-serialization. changing whitespace/ordering affects the key. plus kernel swap changed how KV stores offsets so serialized length/padding shifted -> different hash distribution.

jess: ugh. so two orthogonal things: (1) surface changes to prompt normalization and (2) different serialization/layout from kernel/runtime. both can cause cache misses. quick pragmatic fixes: canonicalize JSON tool/function fields by sorting keys and normalize zws before hashing. low-risk, quick. example normalizer: 
```
def normalize_prefix(s):
    # strip zero-width chars, stable-json, collapse whitespace
    s = re.sub(r"[\u200B-\u200D\uFEFF]", "", s)
    obj = json.loads(s) if looks_like_json(s) else s
    if isinstance(obj, dict):
        s = json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, separators=(",",":"))
    return s.strip()
```

perf-bot: bench report attached: 
- route /chat/compose: hit-rate 78% -> 44%
- route /tools/run: hit-rate 66% -> 28%
- avg KV bytes/prefix: 2.1KB -> 3.4KB
- p50 latency (prefilled): 85ms -> 96ms
- estimated extra token cost/day: ~8% on these routes

miguel: sorting JSON keys sounds ok for tool fields, but can we rely on safe parsing for every prefix? some prefixes are partial multi-part messages.

sam: alternative longer-term fix: compute cache key from the token ID sequence (stable tokenizer-pinned ids) instead of the post-serialization string. that avoids differences introduced by whitespace normalization and runtime serializer alignment. catch: we must include tokenizer version and model version in the key. also requires a fast path to avoid tokenizing twice during hot paths.

anna: agreed. immediate plan: 1) roll out prefix normalizer for tool fields (jess will own PR) 2) add deploy-time warmup job that replays the top-N prefixes across new kernel configs so their KV entries are recreated under the new serializer layout 3) start a short project to switch keying to token-id-hash with explicit tokenizer pins.

jess: I can push the normalizer PR today. for warmup I'm thinking a staged probe: sample top 5k prefixes per region, replay with the new runtime in canary for 1 hour, measure fill-rate and hit-rate delta.

miguel: cost question — warmup will burn GPU cycles. can we TTL warmup entries to avoid long tail costs? sampling top prefixes + TTL 6h sounds fine to me.

sam: small nit: when we compute a token-id-based key, include a short canonical prefix fingerprint (first 32 token ids) rather than whole sequence to keep key size small. also include tokenizer version and kernel-layout tag so we can diagnose later.

perf-bot: quick A/B experiment template created: `perf/kv-warmup/ab-setup-171234` (will post results after run).

deploy-bot: rolling update to runtime-kernel v2.14 started in canary region-1. warmup probe scheduled post-deploy.

anna: thanks all. goals for next steps: jess PR + canary warmup run today, sam and miguel to scope token-id-keying impact. I'll collect baseline + canary metrics after the warmup window and post summary. :thumbsup:
